title: An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
abstract: A Lean 4 proof, conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and on four cited results, that every even integer N at least e^{e^{13.375}} is the sum of a prime and a square-free number greater than 1 with at most two prime factors. The four cited inputs are explicit hypotheses of the theorem, never axioms: Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J, the Lean Lab's transcriptions of Theorems 5, 6 and 7 of M. Bordignon and V. Starichkova, An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Ramanujan J. 64, 2024, 1213 to 1242; and LinearSieveT4 1/8349 112 114, the transcription of their Theorem 4, the explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston and Starichkova with the Table 1 row epsilon inverse 6100, C1 = 112, C2 = 114. In version 2 each of Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J also takes 0 <= C1 and 0 <= C2 as premises right after the sieve hypothesis, matching Table 1, which lists positive constants only. These transcriptions use the Lean normalisation U_N = 2 e^{-gamma} C2 Pi_N, twice the U_N printed in the journal; see the fidelity section. GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is the premise inside the conclusion ChenThreshold13375. The journal's own Corollary 1 has the threshold e^{e^{14}}; the threshold e^{e^{13.375}} comes from re-choosing the Section 5.4 parameters inside the authors' method, alpha = 0.00256, A = 10, u = 1500, epsilon = 1/8349, epsilon1 = 10^-20. The numeric inputs are proved here: epsilon at 1500 is below 1/8349 by a kernel certificate, decide +kernel in eleven window modules, and the Section 5.4 bracket combination is at least the main-term constant minus 10^-5, a one-sided lower bound. Chen's weighted inequality, the journal's Lemma 9, is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote all the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
